description: Agent Onboarding: submit the permissions granted to a new agent and its written job: the job with its id, the written job as given to the agent, read for wording that hands over blanket access such as full access, whatever it needs or same access as, and each system it needs with its id, the system, the level it needs there (read, write or admin) and whether it needs it at all times or only during a task; and each grant with its id, the system it opens, the level (read, write, admin or owner), whether it stays on between tasks and how it was granted (directly, through a role or group, or copied from another agent’s or a person’s access). The signed report gives every grant with the level the job needs on its system and its status as matched, unneeded, above_need, below_need, standing, copied, unrated or unread, every need as granted, missing, under_granted or unrated, and counts the grants matched, unneeded, above the need and copied and the needs missing, and names excessive permissions: a grant on a system the written job does not list, admin or owner rights above the job’s need, a grant copied from another agent’s or a person’s access and blanket wording in the written job; then write where the job only reads, a standing grant the job needs only during a task, a need with no grant and a grant below the need, with the fix for each. No list of needs or an unstated level leaves the permissions unchecked. This reads the permissions granted at joining against the written job, not one action’s authority: whether an actor’s access fits its authority grant for an action is wever_authority-scope-check, a delegation’s written bounds are wever_delegation-scope-check, a stored grant evaluated for an exact subject, action and resource is wever_agent-permission-ledger, a trading or treasury mandate is issued and read with the mandate tools such as wever_mandate-status, which endpoints agents can call is wever_tool-exposure-check and which permissions rest on the model is wever_enforcement-layer-check. Verdict onboarding_permissions_excessive, onboarding_permissions_partial, onboarding_permissions_unchecked or onboarding_permissions_matched. POST /api/onboarding-permissions-check. Reads only the recorded onboarding material in the call: no network request, fetch, money movement, message, configuration change or external write; no credential is issued, rotated or revoked, no permission granted or removed, no wallet funded or moved, no limit set and the agent is not approved, and a credential found in supplied text is named by kind and never repeated. Agent Onboarding reads the setup of a new agent joining a system, before its first task: whether its identity is established and tied to its owner, whether its credentials are scoped to its job, stored where they belong and kept out of prompts, logs and shared documents, whether its wallet is the right one, funded only to the job with recovery recorded by the owner before funds move, whether its permissions match the written job, whether its limits sit in code with a human handoff, whether the systems it needs are provisioned and tested, whether it is ready for its first task and whether the onboarding record matches what is live. It is not vetting an outside party (wever_counterparty-onboarding-check reads a counterparty’s onboarding packet before the system transacts with it; an onboarding check reads an agent joining the system itself), not a grant or an authority for one action (wever_consent-scope-check reads whether a principal’s grant covers a use and wever_authority-scope-check whether an actor’s access fits its grant for an action; an onboarding check reads that the grant and the authority were put in place before the first task, and does not re-check them per action), not a limit in flight (the wever_limit checks and wever_agent-budget-guard read limits for work already running; an onboarding check reads that limits were set in code before it starts) and not an action’s consequences (the wever_risk checks read one planned action; an onboarding check reads readiness to start). Paid URL: 0.10 USDC per call on Base via x402 exact, with the shared 10 signed-wallet free calls per rolling 30 days. Bind X-Wever-Wallet-Proof to the exact JSON arguments and the tool route. Returns a report with an Ed25519 signed receipt. Contract: /api/agent-onboarding-contract. Human page: https://weverlabs.com/agent-onboarding/.

granted.description: Each permission granted to the agent; empty when none.

id.description: The grant id, such as g1.

level.description: The level granted: read, write, admin or owner.

standing.description: The grant stays on between tasks rather than being issued per task.

via.description: How it was granted: directly, through a role or group, or copied from another agent’s or a person’s access.

needs.description: Each system the written job needs, with the level it needs.

id.description: The need id, such as n1.

when.description: Whether the job needs it at all times or only during a task.

text.description: The written job as given to the agent, read for wording that hands over blanket access, such as full access or whatever it needs.

label.description: Optional name recorded in the report.

title: Onboarding permissions check
